A timeline showing the evolution of suffrage in Nigeria. 1922: A formally dressed wealthy man in Lagos dropping a ballot into a box (Clifford Constitution, limited franchise). 1951/54: A larger group of men voting in different regions (expanding franchise). 1979: A diverse queue of Nigerian men and women, including women in hijab from the North, voting together (Universal Adult Suffrage).

A flowchart of the electoral process from start to finish. Boxes connected by arrows: 1. Delimitation of Constituencies -> 2. Voter Registration -> 3. Party Primaries -> 4. Political Campaigns -> 5. Accreditation & Voting -> 6. Counting & Collation -> 7. Declaration of Results. Use clean flat textbook style, white background, with a small relevant icon in each box (e.g., a map for delimitation, a megaphone for campaigns, a ballot box for voting).

A comparative graphic showing FPTP vs Proportional Representation (PR). On the left (FPTP): A bar chart where Party A gets 40% of votes but takes 100% of a district's single seat (a large trophy icon). On the right (PR): A pie chart of votes (Party A 40%, Party B 35%, Party C 25%) next to a Parliament seating chart colored exactly to match the pie chart (40% blue seats, 35% red seats, 25% green seats).
